transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has not decided yet whether he will order new attacks on Iran.
That's according to comments over the weekend by Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
NPR's Ea Betrawi reports Arab states are backing diplomatic efforts to stave off more fighting.
Qatari mediators are working with Iran on a two-day plan that would halt attacks on ships
in the Strait of Hormuz and lay the ground for direct U.S.-Iran talks again.
But some Gulf Arab partners have also been told to prepare for powerful U.S. attacks
on Iran soon.
UAE diplomat Anwar Gargash told a security forum in Bahrain that countries here don't
want that.
From the perspective of the UAE, and I would also say Gulf countries, we don't really
want to see another round of confrontation in the region.
Iran's vowed powerful counter-blows if it's attacked.
Ea Betrawi, NPR News, Manama Bahrain.
President Trump is set to deliver remarks this afternoon at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting
Pool.
NPR's Chamor Keith reports this is where he'll make his final pitch to voters for the midterms.
The Reflecting Pool was the backdrop for Martin Luther King's I Have a Dream speech in 1963.
But this year it was at the heart of controversy, as President Trump boasted about its restoration,
before falsely blaming vandalism for what the Justice Department later admitted was
actually a rushed and botched job.
Repairs are now completed.
A White House official tells NPR Trump's remarks will focus on "restoring our great
capital" and also a closing message before the midterms about what the administration
and Republicans in Congress accomplished over the past two years.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
Michigan Democratic Congresswoman Hailey Stevens has revoked her endorsement of Democratic
Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
Instead, she is endorsing Republican Mike Rogers.
Stevens lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed earlier this year.
She says El-Sayed has not done enough to distance himself from an outside ad critical of Israel.
Florida authorities say all nine people aboard a small business jet were killed when it plunged
into a neighborhood.
Yesterday, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis says the jet lost altitude and crashed not far
from Miami.
Obviously, this was a cataclysmic plane crash.
It looked like a missile going down.
It left a big crater on the side of the road.
The jet had departed Austin, Texas, and was headed for the Bahamas.
The National Transportation Safety Board will investigate.
There are flood watches and warnings up in the Four Corners area.
Heavy storms have poured a lot of rain on parts of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and
Utah.
Flooding rivers have triggered evacuations.
You're listening to NPR.
There appears to be another cyberattack underway against refrigerators and freezers in some
European countries.
Because of grocery stores in Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg say the temperatures in some
of their freezers are spiking to more than 120 degrees.
There was a similar cyberattack last month in France.
The U.S. Capitol Christmas tree that was harvested in north Idaho last month is now making its
way to Washington, D.C.
Lauren Patterson of Boise State Public Radio was at one of the tree's first whistle stops
in Arofino, Idaho yesterday.
The 76-foot-tall U.S. Capitol Christmas tree has been encased in the back of a big semi-truck.
But the top is made of wooden beams and glass so people can see the colorful lights and
handmade ornaments covering the green spruce branches.
The whistle stop tour turned the local grocery store parking lot into a hub of activity with
people of all ages.
Many of the locals have come out to see and take pictures with the tree.
Christy Skinner is one of them.
When we get to turn the TV on on Christmas and New Year's and watch it, they'd be just
really proud to know that it came from Europe.
The tree has more scheduled whistle stops throughout Idaho, Montana, Wyoming and the Midwest before
arriving at its final destination.
For NPR News, I'm Lauren Patterson in Arofino, Idaho.
A British man who's been walking around the world for nearly 30 years has arrived back
at his mother's home in England.
Carl Buschby walked 31,000 miles over four continents and 30 countries and avoided taking
transport.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump has not decided on new attacks on Iran; Qatari mediators push a two-day plan on Hormuz
Trump to speak at Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, final midterm pitch after repair controversy
Michigan Rep. Hailey Stevens revokes endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed, endorses Mike Rogers
Nine killed when small business jet crashes into Florida neighborhood near Miami; NTSB investigating
Flood watches and warnings across Four Corners region after heavy storms in Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, Utah
Cyberattack apparently spikes freezer temperatures at grocery stores in Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg
U.S. Capitol Christmas tree begins whistle-stop tour in Idaho en route to Washington, D.C.
British man Carl Buschby returns to England after walking 31,000 miles around the world over nearly 30 years
